transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for making time to discuss the eighth-grade civics oral-history project. Before I can sign off on this, I need to make sure we've addressed the key requirements in the approval packet. I'd like to hear from each of you -- the project advisor, our counselor, and our instructional technology coordinator -- regarding your findings and any concerns. Let's start with an overview of the project plan and then work through each area. Who would like to begin?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. I'm happy to give an overview of the project plan. As you know, our eighth-grade civics class has proposed an oral-history project where students will interview community members about local history. The current draft plan calls for 20 student interviewers, audio recording on personal phones, publication of all recordings on the public school website, and indefinite retention of the files. Before we go further, I do have an important finding from my project roster review that I'd like to share with the group, as it directly affects the interviewer plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. I'd like to share my findings from the family-consent review. My review confirms that interviewees I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive, and the plan must include a consent-exclusion record. This means the current draft plan's call for publication of all recordings on the public school website would need to be modified to exclude these five interviewees' recordings from public publication.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. I'd like to share my findings from the technology review. My review confirms that personal phones cannot be used for school recordings. The project must use district tablets, store the source files in the restricted OralHistory drive, and delete recordings exactly 45 days after the final class presentation. Storing source files in that drive does not prohibit publishing consented recordings on the public school website. Additionally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record. This means the current draft plan's use of personal phones and indefinite retention would both need to be modified.
